status: draft: not frozen; no training has run
data: synthetic everywhere; nothing here is market data

paper.source: Acero, Plank and Zhang, arXiv:2610.16524v1, single-asset experiments (Table 1)
paper.data: synthetic: two independent Hawkes processes of market orders, a Brownian mid with zero direct impact, exponential fill probability; the paper's setting as its text gives it, apart from our simulator

parameters.rule: each arm's policy and value MLPs have two hidden layers of one width, the integer width whose trainable parameter count is nearest the target; it must fall within the tolerance

reproduction.statistic: two-sided Welch t-test of HSN against the best control by mean, over the 30 training seeds' mean objectives, as the paper reports
reproduction.rule: a row reproduces when the observed class equals the paper's: tie when p >= 0.05; hsn_better when HSN's mean is above the best control's and p < 0.05; hsn_worse otherwise

choices: The paper does not give n_epochs; SB3's default of 10 is used.

The paper maps the policy output to the spread range by a sigmoid; here the Gaussian is over the raw output in [-10, 10], which the trainer clips, and the environment applies the sigmoid. The initial log standard deviation is SB3's 0.
One fill is one unit. At Q = 5 the bid does not fill and at Q = -5 the ask does not; the order is still observed.
The step reward is the change of X + Q S minus gamma Q^2 dt, and the last step adds -kappa Q_T^2, so rewards sum exactly to the paper's objective.

A step runs from one decision to the next market order; the first decision is at t = 0 and the episode ends at T. There is no warm-up history: an episode starts with no past events, as the paper describes none.
Events are simulated by Ogata thinning, exact for non-increasing kernels. Every draw of an episode comes from its seed before the first step, so every arm meets the same episodes.
Each buffered event is its age and its side one-hot. The paper's frame-stack uses (dt, side); age carries the same information.
The scalar state is (S - S0) / (sigma sqrt T), Q / 5 and (T - t) / T.
Head widths come from the parameter rule, not the paper's per-arm widths, which do not give its stated counts under SB3's separate policy and value MLPs.
The Transformer baseline is not run: the issue asks for MLP, EMA and recurrent controls.
The paper's evaluation seeds are not given; seeds 1000000 to 1000099 are used for every arm.

causal.data: synthetic: Hawkes market orders from examples/hawkes_days.rs moving the mid by a linear impact plus a diffusion; made-up parameters
causal.seed: 1000003 + day for the day's flow (buy side 2 x seed, sell side 2 x seed + 1) and diffusion, the same in every setting
